LESSON: LABOUR RELATIONS IN ISLAM

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalat
Topic 6.3: Labour Relations in Islam
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Labour Relations in Islam, part of Muamalat in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to have good labour relations in work place?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the conditions for a valid labour contract according to Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Labour Relations in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the rights of employer and employee in Islam for conducive working environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Labour Relations in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Labour Relations in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of having good relationship between employer and employee.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Labour Relations in Islam in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the conditions for a valid labour contract according to Islam,

   Labour Relations in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. examine the rights of employer and employee in Islam for conducive working environment,

   Labour Relations in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam,

   Labour Relations in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the importance of having good relationship between employer and employee.

   Labour Relations in Islam helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or on available reference materials on the conditions for a governing labour contract, make notes and present in class,

2. carry out a project on the rights of employer and employee and make class presentation, learners with blindness can be given physical support as they carry out the project,

3. listen to a resource person giving a talk on suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam and make notes,

4. dramatise relationship between employer and employee, learners with

A. At school

1. search online or on available reference materials on the conditions for a governing labour contract, make notes and present in class,
2. carry out a project on the rights of employer and employee and make class presentation, learners with blindness can be given physical support as they carry out the project,
3. listen to a resource person giving a talk on suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam and make notes,
4. dramatise relationship between employer and employee, learners with

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Labour Relations in Islam together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: the skills of interacting with digital technology and connecting with technology enhanced as learners search

online or on available reference materials on the conditions for a governing labour contract

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the skills of evaluation and decision making enhanced as learners listen to a

resource person giving a talk on suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking enhanced as learners dramatise relationship between employer and

employee

● Citizenship: active community skill enhanced as learners carry out a project on the rights of employer and employee

Values:
● Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners carry out a project on the rights of employer and employee

● Respect: human dignity enhanced as learners carry out a project on the rights of employer and employee

• Unity: cooperation, fairness and non-discrimination enhanced as learners work collaboratively dramatise relationship

between employer and employee

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship education: Protection from inhuman treatment and punishment

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. explain the conditions for a valid labour contract according to Islam,
2. examine the rights of employer and employee in Islam for conducive working environment,
3. suggest mechanisms of resolving disputes between employer and employee in Islam,
4. appreciate the importance of having good relationship between employer and employee.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to have good labour relations in work place?
